part.text:
## Summary

Refactored the SSG into a plugin-driven architecture while keeping every existing export byte-for-byte compatible:

- **`src/plugin.ts`** — `Plugin` interface (`onStart`/`beforeBuild`/`onFile`/`afterBuild`/`onEnd`, all optional) and `PluginContext`.
- **`src/engine.ts`** — `SSGEngine` orchestrates the pipeline: each stage runs every plugin's hook in list order before advancing; `onFile` runs the full plugin chain per page. `runSync()` (throws if a plugin returns a Promise) backs the legacy synchronous `buildSite()`; `run()` is the async version for pipelines with async plugins.
- **`src/plugins/`** — built-ins: `markdownPlugin.ts` (loads/parses content in `beforeBuild`), `templatePlugin.ts` (renders + writes pages/index/stylesheet), `devServerPlugin.ts` (starts the live-reload server in `onEnd`), each just a thin wrapper around the untouched `parser.ts`/`templateEngine.ts`/`templates.ts`/`devServer.ts`.
- **`src/config.ts`** — `loadConfig()` loads `ssg.config.ts` at runtime via a `require.extensions('.ts')` hook built on the TypeScript compiler API (no `ts-node` needed); moved `typescript` to a runtime dependency for this.
- **`src/generator.ts`** — `buildSite()` now just builds `SSGEngine([markdownPlugin, templatePlugin]).runSync(options)` — same signature, same synchronous behavior, same output.
- **`src/cli.ts`** — added an opt-in `--config <path>` flag on `build` that runs the async plugin pipeline; omitting it preserves the exact old behavior.
- **`ssg.config.ts` + `plugins/exampleLoggerPlugin.ts`** — example of a user-authored plugin wired through config, verified working end-to-end via a manual smoke test.

All 8 original test files are untouched and pass unmodified; added `tests/pluginSystem.test.ts` covering hook ordering, sync/async engines, page transforms, the dev-server plugin, and config loading.
